root_cause.text: In the `weighted_interleave_auto_store()` function within `mm/mempolicy.c`, the retrieval of the previous state (`old_wi_state`) was incorrectly scoped inside the `if (!input)` conditional block, preventing proper deallocation of the newly allocated `new_wi_state` or the existing RCU-managed `old_wi_state` pointer depending on the input value.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff moves `old_wi_state = rcu_dereference_protected(wi_state, ...)` outside the `if (!input)` block to ensure unconditional fetching, while the CVE description confirms this scoping error caused memory leaks when users wrote "true" (skipping old state free) or "false" with matching mode (skipping new state free).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leak by adding kfree() for new_wi_state in early return path and restructure control flow for clearer null-pointer handling.
intent_record.what: Restructured conditional logic in weighted_interleave_auto_store: moved rcu_dereference_protected call outside the !input block, added kfree(new_wi_state) before early return when input matches old_wi_state->mode_auto, and simplified the nested if conditions.
intent_record.how: Ensures new_wi_state memory is properly freed when returning early due to unchanged mode_auto setting, preventing a memory leak. Also ensures old_wi_state is always accessed regardless of input value, making the null-check logic more explicit.

Group 0 explicitly aims to fix this memory leak by adding kfree() calls and restructuring control flow, directly addressing the allocation/deallocation logic error identified in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement declares both new_wi_state and old_wi_state pointers. According to the root cause, the subsequent retrieval/scoping of old_wi_state was incorrectly placed inside an if (!input) conditional block, preventing proper deallocation of either the newly allocated new_wi_state or the existing RCU-managed old_wi_state pointer when input is true and early return conditions fail.
